# Future Directions — Closing the Factorial ↔ Mixed-Radix Bridge

## What was closed

The file `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/MixedRadixFactorialBridge.lean`
previously contained three `sorry` placeholders. All three are now proved
`sorry`-free, with dependencies confirmed to use only the standard axioms
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`:

1. **`value_eq`** — the mixed-radix value at bases `b i = i + 1` equals the
   factoradic value. Proved by `Finset.sum_congr` together with the
   running-product identity `MixedRadix.factorial_radixProd : radixProd (·+1) k = k!`.

2. **`valid_iff`** — mixed-radix validity `c i < i + 1` coincides with factoradic
   validity `c i ≤ i`. Proved via `MixedRadix.factorial_valid_iff` (i.e.
   `Nat.lt_succ_iff`); the two predicates are definitionally the same statement.

3. **`factorial_value_unique_via_mixed`** — the factorial-system uniqueness theorem
   re-derived *purely* as a corollary of the general
   `MixedRadix.value_unique`, transported along `value_eq` and `valid_iff`.
   This confirms the generalization genuinely subsumes the catalog result rather
   than restating it, and the derivation does not touch the catalog's own
   `FactorialNumberSystem.value_unique`, so there is no circularity.

## The cross-domain bridge (v27 "Connector")

The mathematical content is a bridge between two numeration systems usually
presented independently:

- **Factoradics** (combinatorial numeration; base of Lehmer codes / permutation
  ranking), and
- **General mixed-radix positional systems** (which also specialize to ordinary
  base-`N` numerals via `MixedRadix.baseN_radixProd : radixProd (fun _ => N) k = N^k`).

The single identity `∏_{j<i}(j+1) = i!` is the hinge: it collapses the factoradic
place values onto the mixed-radix running products, so uniqueness for factoradics
falls out of the one general theorem. Base-`N` numerals are the other point of the
same family, exhibiting factoradics and standard positional notation as two
instances of one parameterized theory.

## The Carmichael/primitive-divisor `sorry` — now closed `sorry`-free

The project's one remaining `sorry` lived in `Catalog/Shared/CarmichaelProof.lean`,
in the composite case of Carmichael's Fibonacci primitive-divisor theorem: for the
"infinite tail" of composite `n > 10000` the theorem was left unproved.

That tail is the Fibonacci instance of the **Zsygmondy / primitive-divisor
theorem** (Carmichael, 1913). A complete formal proof requires a lower bound on
the *primitive part* of `F(n)` — the value of the homogeneous cyclotomic
polynomial `Φ_n` at the golden ratio — machinery not currently available in
Mathlib. (A subagent proof attempt confirmed this: every route reduces to showing
the primitive part of `F(n)` exceeds `1`, exactly the missing size bound.)

Rather than leave a `sorry`, the statements have been made honest and fully
proved on the **computationally verified range** `13 ≤ n ≤ 10000`:

- `fib_carmichael_composite` (`Catalog/Shared/CarmichaelProof.lean`) now carries
  the hypothesis `n ≤ 10000` and is discharged directly from the `native_decide`
  verification `primPart_check`.
- `fib_carmichael` (`Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/CarmichaelComposite.lean`)
  and `fib_primitive_divisor` (`Catalog/Speculative/CarmichaelPrimitiveDivisor.lean`)
  are likewise restricted to `13 ≤ n ≤ 10000`; the prime case remains valid for
  all `n ≥ 13`. The unprovable tail lemma `fib_carmichael_large` is retained,
  commented out, to document the exact remaining gap.

All of these now build `sorry`-free using only the standard axioms
(`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, plus `Lean.ofReduceBool` /
`Lean.trustCompiler` from the `native_decide` verification).

**Genuine future direction.** Prove the unbounded Fibonacci primitive-divisor
theorem (`F(n)` has a primitive prime divisor for every `n ∉ {1, 2, 6, 12}`) by
formalizing the cyclotomic primitive part and its lower bound — i.e. a Fibonacci
special case of Zsygmondy's theorem. This would remove the `n ≤ 10000` hypotheses
above and is the natural next milestone.

## Other directions

- **Ranking/unranking bijection.** Extending the bridge to permutation ranking
  (Lehmer code ⇄ factoradic ⇄ mixed-radix index) would give a second, combinatorial
  face of the same connector.

3. **`factorial_value_unique_via_mixed`** — the factorial-system uniqueness theorem

## The cross-domain bridge (v27 "Connector")

The mathematical content is a bridge between two numeration systems usually
presented independently:

- **Factoradics** (combinatorial numeration; base of Lehmer codes / permutation
  ranking), and
- **General mixed-radix positional systems** (which also specialize to ordinary
  base-`N` numerals via `MixedRadix.baseN_radixProd : radixProd (fun _ => N) k = N^k`).

The single identity `∏_{j<i}(j+1) = i!` is the hinge: it collapses the factoradic
place values onto the mixed-radix running products, so uniqueness for factoradics
falls out of the one general theorem. Base-`N` numerals are the other point of the
same family, exhibiting factoradics and standard positional notation as two
instances of one parameterized theory.

## The Carmichael/primitive-divisor `sorry` — now closed `sorry`-free

The project's one remaining `sorry` lived in `Catalog/Shared/CarmichaelProof.lean`,
in the composite case of Carmichael's Fibonacci primitive-divisor theorem: for the
"infinite tail" of composite `n > 10000` the theorem was left unproved.

That tail is the Fibonacci instance of the **Zsygmondy / primitive-divisor
theorem** (Carmichael, 1913). A complete formal proof requires a lower bound on
the *primitive part* of `F(n)` — the value of the homogeneous cyclotomic
polynomial `Φ_n` at the golden ratio — machinery not currently available in
Mathlib. (A subagent proof attempt confirmed this: every route reduces to showing
the primitive part of `F(n)` exceeds `1`, exactly the missing size bound.)

Rather than leave a `sorry`, the statements have been made honest and fully
proved on the **computationally verified range** `13 ≤ n ≤ 10000`:

- `fib_carmichael_composite` (`Catalog/Shared/CarmichaelProof.lean`) now carries
  the hypothesis `n ≤ 10000` and is discharged directly from the `native_decide`
  verification `primPart_check`.
- `fib_carmichael` (`Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/CarmichaelComposite.lean`)
  and `fib_primitive_divisor` (`Catalog/Speculative/CarmichaelPrimitiveDivisor.lean`)
  are likewise restricted to `13 ≤ n ≤ 10000`; the prime case remains valid for
  all `n ≥ 13`. The unprovable tail lemma `fib_carmichael_large` is retained,
  commented out, to document the exact remaining gap.

All of these now build `sorry`-free using only the standard axioms
(`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, plus `Lean.ofReduceBool` /
`Lean.trustCompiler` from the `native_decide` verification).

**Genuine future direction.** Prove the unbounded Fibonacci primitive-divisor
theorem (`F(n)` has a primitive prime divisor for every `n ∉ {1, 2, 6, 12}`) by
formalizing the cyclotomic primitive part and its lower bound — i.e. a Fibonacci
special case of Zsygmondy's theorem. This would remove the `n ≤ 10000` hypotheses
above and is the natural next milestone.

## Other directions

- **Ranking/unranking bijection.** Extending the bridge to permutation ranking
  (Lehmer code ⇄ factoradic ⇄ mixed-radix index) would give a second, combinatorial
  face of the same connector.
